questions.q: In everyday use, why is Add Chart greyed out on a plain tabular report?
options: Tabular reports are read-only
There are no groupings, so there is nothing to aggregate and plot
Charts require a joined report
The user lacks the Dashboard permission
questions.explain: Charts plot grouped, summarized data. A plain list of rows has no groupings, so Add Chart is unavailable in the usual case.

questions.q: In a report chart, what does the X-axis (or the slices of a donut) typically come from?
options: A summarized value such as Sum of Amount
A grouping in the report, such as Lead Source
A filter in the Filters panel
The report's folder name
questions.explain: Categories come from groupings; the measured size or height comes from a summarized value.

questions.q: Which report characteristic makes a stacked or grouped chart possible?
options: A locked filter
A row limit
A bucket column on a text field
A second grouping, as in a matrix report
questions.explain: Stacked and grouped series need two dimensions, so the report needs a second grouping, such as a matrix's row and column groupings.

questions.q: How many charts can a single Salesforce report hold?
options: One
Up to three
One per grouping
As many as fit on screen
questions.explain: A report holds a single chart. To show several visuals of the same data, use a dashboard with multiple components.

questions.q: You want a chart to show a win-rate measure that is not yet on the report. What should you do first?
options: Add the measure to the report, for example as a summary formula, then chart it
Type the value directly into the chart properties
Change the chart to a table
Create a new dashboard filter
questions.explain: A chart can only plot what the report groups and summarizes, so add the measure to the report first.
